terms.meaning: the chance of each possible ball result, such as a dot, a single, a four, a six or a wicket
a fingerprint of a file's contents, used to detect changes

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup and sample loading
sections.what: Imports the test tools, the outcome labels, the outcome model functions and the chase loader. Reads the saved outcome model and, before the tests run, loads all chase samples once with a one-minute time limit.
sections.why: Loading the samples once saves time across all the tests in the file.
sections.watch_out: The one-minute limit can be reached on a slow machine, which would stop the tests before they start.

sections.name: per-ball outcome model (outcomes) (part 1)
sections.title: Checks the per-ball outcome tables
sections.what: Checks that every outcome table covers the same results (0 to 6 runs and a wicket) and that each table adds up to 100 percent. It also checks that the model trains on older seasons and holds back the latest three, that a fitted file matches its stored fingerprint, and that the cricket patterns look right (more sixes when the rate is steep, more wickets late in the innings). Finally it checks that a real 2008 chase is turned into correct ball-by-ball states.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The test names suggest they guard against a fitted model that is wrong without any visible error.
sections.watch_out: The fingerprint test refits the model and compares hashes, so any change to the fitting code will fail it until the saved model file is regenerated.

sections.name: per-ball outcome model (outcomes) (part 2)
sections.title: Checks how wides, no-balls and wickets carry forward
sections.what: Checks that extras such as wides do not use up a legal ball, so the next legal ball carries the state forward. It also checks that deliveries recorded after the chase is decided are ignored, and that a few helper functions return the expected values.
sections.why: Likely reason: in cricket a wide does not count as a ball faced, so the model must skip it when counting balls left.
sections.watch_out: Deliveries after the target is passed are dropped on purpose, so a faulty data feed with extra deliveries will not show up as an error here.

summary: Checks the per-ball outcome model: its hash, its training on past seasons, and how it learns from chase data. Only the setup part is described here.
purpose: Makes sure the per-ball model used across the app is versioned, reproducible and trained on valid samples.
why: Reason not stated in the code for the rest of the file, because only its setup is shown.
how: Loads the saved outcome model and builds the list of chase samples once before the tests run, with a one-minute time limit.
inputs: data/models/outcomes-v1.json and the loader in scripts/fit-outcomes.
outputs: Test results. The setup itself produces the sample list used by the tests.
risks: Loading samples can be slow. On a slow machine, the one-minute limit can be reached.
debug: If setup times out or fails, check that the saved file exists and that the fit script's loader runs.
